newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher across the board on Sunday with high and active demand for most bonds, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 to 104.83

"There were rises across the board. Yields of the different bonds are similar and traders are buying all kinds of bonds to be secured from all sides," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.

"Prices rose in all the CPI-linked bonds but in particular in the long-term bonds which rose by about 0.25 percent. Traders are expecting yields of these bonds to fall because of reports that in April there was a budget surplus. This means the government will issue less bonds and there will be less supply in the market causing prices to rise," he said.
Israel posted a total budget surplus of 341 million shekels in April, preliminary figures released by the Treasury on Thursday showed.

"Some traders believe future consumer price indices will be lower and so they buy unlinked bonds. Others still fear a rising inflation and are buying CPI-linked bonds. The prices of these CPI-linked bonds have been going up also because the Treasury is issuing less of these bonds," said Ilan Doron of Solid Capital Markets.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
